clue.text: Assistant, one backing stylish Fiat?

parts.note: to second a motion or a duellist is to back them, and the person doing it is a second
in fashion, as in 'the in thing'
a fiat is an authoritative order or decree

explanation.surface: Someone helping out, perhaps a mechanic, supports a fashionable little Italian car.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiat looks like the Italian carmaker, but here it is the ordinary word for a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: The deputy who ranks directly below a leader is that leader's chief helper and stand-in.

clue.text: Star, Moon and Newton in Brian Cox show

parts.note: a star is a big hit, a success
Io is one of the moons of Jupiter
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Physicist Brian Cox presents a science programme about stars, the Moon and Isaac Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Brian Cox the physicist and TV presenter; the answer is the drama starring Brian Cox the Scottish actor, who played Logan Roy.
explanation.definitionFit: The HBO drama about the Roy media dynasty starred the actor of that name as its patriarch.

clue.text: Brief opportunity to meet Queen perhaps in Minister's office

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the following word loses its final letter

parts.note: a synonym
Ellery Queen is the fictional detective and pen name of two American crime writers; 'perhaps' flags one Ellery as an example

explanation.surface: A minister snatches a brief chance to meet the monarch in their office.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks like royalty, but it is the surname that goes with the first name wanted here.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancellery is the official building or department of a chancellor, a senior government minister.

clue.text: Tight on a motorway, two Sierras in close call

parts.note: near means stingy, tight with money
the M1 is a British motorway, with the 1 read as the letter I
Sierra is the radio code word for S, and two of them give a pair

explanation.surface: Two Ford Sierras driving too close together on a motorway nearly crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra was a popular Ford car, which fits the motorway scene, but here it is the NATO alphabet word for S.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident narrowly avoided is a close shave, the same idea as a lucky escape.

clue.text: Local IT system on the way, second one to be replaced by base

indicators.note: one thing being replaced by another means letters are swapped out of the phrase and new ones put in their place

parts.note: something on its way is in transit
S is the abbreviation for second
I is the Roman numeral for one
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Instructions for a company's computer network being upgraded, with a component swapped for a new base unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Second and one together are the S and I in the middle of the phrase; both go, and the single letter for the base takes their place.
explanation.definitionFit: An intranet is a private computer network used only within one organisation, not open to the wider internet.

clue.text: Nancy's good at the end of Coach C

parts.note: a coach on a train is a railway car
Nancy is a city in France, so its word for good is the French one

explanation.surface: Someone called Nancy did well at the end of a coaching course and earned a C grade.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy reads as a woman's name but is the French city, signalling a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: C is the chemical symbol for the element found in coal, diamond and graphite.

clue.text: Grasp head

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to learn something thoroughly, as a verb
second meaning: the person in charge, as in the head of a school or a ship's captain

explanation.definitionFit: To get the hang of a skill fully is to master it, and a master is also the chief or principal of something.

clue.text: Mock adult prior to school lesson

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film classification
physical education, a school subject

explanation.surface: A grown-up pokes fun at children before their lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate them, often in a mocking, parodying way.

clue.text: Matt Damon's first to accompany actress Tracey, taking crew out

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the initial of the name is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Damon

indicators.note: taking something out of a name removes those letters from it, here a word meaning crew

parts.note: Tracey Ullman is a British comic actress
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: Matt Damon co-stars with Tracey Ullman, but the film crew are cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Matt is a first name in the surface, but it is the definition, meaning not shiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A matt finish lacks shine or gloss, so it looks lacklustre and flat.

clue.text: Nature of tea tree covering Thailand's capital

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: something covering another wraps round it, so the tree word goes around a letter

parts.note: an acer is a maple tree

indicators.note: a word's capital is its head or initial, so only the first letter of the country is used

parts.note: the initial of Thailand

explanation.surface: A question about the nature of a tea plantation in Thailand, shaded by trees around Bangkok.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital suggests Bangkok, but it only asks for the first letter of Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's character is their essential temperament or disposition, their basic make-up.

clue.text: Great snowball

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excellent, in dated slang, as an adjective
second meaning: to grow rapidly, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned slang uses the word for something splendid, and as a verb it means to increase or build up quickly.

clue.text: Acting in cameo, getting compliments

indicators.note: acting means putting on a performance, so the words that follow play a different role and change their order

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: An actor who plays a brief cameo part still gets glowing reviews.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomia is the plural of encomium, a formal speech or piece of writing praising someone highly.

clue.text: Nervous round Kelly maybe, close to scoring against Spain

parts.note: O is round in shape
Ned Kelly was the Australian outlaw; 'maybe' marks him as one example of the name

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, so only its last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of scoring
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A footballer called Kelly is jittery, nearly scoring in a match against Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelly is a surname in the surface; here it is the first name of the famous bushranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for feeling tense, anxious and jumpy.

clue.text: Bird on a ledge, leg out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the preceding letters must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A bird perched on a cliff ledge sticks its leg out.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden eagle is a large bird of prey that nests on mountain crags and cliff ledges.

clue.text: Imagines fiend is caught by weapons without resistance

parts.note: a fiend can be an enthusiast or fanatic, as in a fitness fiend

indicators.note: being caught by something means being held inside it, so the little word sits within the weapons
without means lacking, so the weapons word loses a letter standing for resistance

parts.note: Tasers are electric stun guns
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demon is captured with stun guns that meet no resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiend suggests a devil, but it is used in its sense of a keen devotee.
explanation.definitionFit: To fantasise is to daydream or picture things in the mind that are not real.

clue.text: Hack and news chief checking page is displayed prominently

indicators.note: checking means holding back or blocking, so the cutting word holds a letter inside it

parts.note: to hack is to cut or slash
P is the abbreviation for page
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A reporter and his editor check the page where a story is given big headline treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack looks like a journalist, fitting the newsroom, but it means to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A story splashed across a newspaper is given big, eye-catching front-page coverage.

clue.text: Jumper, something Rowan has back to front

indicators.note: back to front here means the letter at the back is moved round to the front

parts.note: a rowan is a tree, and trees have leaves

explanation.surface: A sweater that someone called Rowan wears back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper is the British word for a sweater, which Rowan seems to wear the wrong way round; here it means an insect that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny wingless insect is famous for leaping enormous distances relative to its size.

clue.text: Promise to quit cycling sports on holiday?

indicators.note: cycling means going round in a loop, so a letter travels from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
someone on holiday is off work

explanation.surface: A resolution to give up cycling and other sports while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling looks like the sport, but it tells you to move the last letter of the word for sports to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear off something is to vow solemnly to give it up, typically a habit like drinking.

clue.text: On the water having abandoned port etc?

definitions.text: On the water having abandoned port etc?

parts.words: On the water having abandoned port etc?
parts.note: surface reading: a ship at sea having sailed out of harbour

parts.words: On the water having abandoned port etc?
parts.note: setter's reading: drinking only water, having given up port wine and other alcohol

explanation.surface: A ship has left its harbour and is out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains completely from alcohol drinks only soft drinks, having renounced wine and spirits.

clue.text: Obvious toupee, periodically new

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of toupee
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A hairpiece that is plain for all to see, and new from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open is in plain view, not hidden or secret, so it is evident.

clue.text: Dessert in pâtisserie is most delightful

parts.note: sweet is the British word for a pudding course
pâtisserie is a French word, signalling French, and est is French for is

explanation.surface: A dessert in a French cake shop is the most delicious thing on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of an adjective meaning charming or pleasing gives the most charming of all.

clue.text: Awful what barrister tipped for buffet

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the following word is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: tipped means tipped over, so in this down clue the lawyer's letters are turned upside down

parts.note: a KC, King's Counsel, is a senior barrister

explanation.surface: A lawyer was given an awful tip for a buffet meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffet looks like a spread of food, but it is a verb meaning to strike. A barrister is a British courtroom lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to strike or batter repeatedly, and a hard sharp blow is a wallop.

clue.text: College's ball precedes November concert

parts.note: uni is short for university, here with the possessive s
O is shaped like a ball
November is the radio code word for N

explanation.surface: A university ball takes place before a November concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Concert reads as a musical event, but it is the abstract noun for agreement, as in acting in concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison means simultaneous agreement or harmony, the same as acting in concert together.

clue.text: Joining 9 in bar-room?

parts.note: surface reading: someone with personality, the answer to 9, joining the drinkers in a pub
setter's reading: a typographical symbol, as 9's answer can mean, that links the two halves of the printed word bar-room

explanation.surface: A colourful personality joins the regulars in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: This short dash is a punctuation mark used to link the parts of a compound word.

clue.text: Simple Simon was so alone!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: naive and without guile
second meaning, read cryptically: Paul Simon without his singing partner Art Garfunkel

explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Simple Simon of the nursery rhyme, but the Simon meant is Paul Simon of Simon & Garfunkel.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means innocent and unsophisticated, lacking cunning or deceit.

clue.text: Sports editor somewhat upset one day, long ago

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in this down clue the letters are read from bottom to top
somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the run of letters is taken

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A sports editor was mildly annoyed about something that happened one day long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides was a single date in the old Roman calendar, so the plural-looking word fits 'one day'; it is famous from the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome this was a fixed day in the middle of each month, such as the 15th of March.

clue.text: Teaching trick with great magician's advice, first of all

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or trick them

indicators.note: first of all means the first letter of every one of the words just before it

parts.note: the opening letters of great, magician's and advice

explanation.surface: A conjuring trick taught with a famous magician's guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: Trick looks like part of the magic act, but it gives a short slang verb for swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true, a doctrine.

clue.text: Slush fund ultimately excluded from capital

indicators.note: excluded from means kept out of, so that letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: capital, as an old-fashioned exclamation, means excellent or good

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of fund

explanation.surface: A secret slush fund is finally shut out of the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Slush fund reads as one phrase, but slush is the definition on its own; capital is the old 'Capital!' meaning splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is sticky, sloppy or mushy stuff, like half-melted snow; it also means sentimentality, as slush can.

clue.text: Deficiencies in footwear, requiring right label inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the two short pieces go into the footwear word

parts.note: a synonym
R is the abbreviation for right
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Faulty shoes need the correct label sewn inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortages are situations where there is not enough of something, so they are lacks or insufficiencies.

clue.text: Noel presents Legs & Co. and flirts zanily, entertaining family

indicators.note: entertaining guests means holding them in, so the jumble wraps round the word for relations
zanily means in a crazy, clownish way, so the letters before it are thrown about

parts.note: the letters of the name, ignoring the ampersand and full stop
taken as written
kin are relatives, one's family

explanation.surface: TV host Noel Edmonds introduces the dance troupe Legs & Co, who flirt madly and entertain the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Legs & Co was the female dance troupe on the BBC's Top of the Pops; Noel looks like Noel Edmonds, but here it means Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Small gifts put in a Christmas stocking are given at Yuletide, Noel being another word for that season.
